newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Fudosan says loss report speculative.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Fudosan says loss report speculative.

text.p: Mitsui Fudosan Co Ltd said on Thursday that a newspaper report saying it was expected to post a parent current loss of more than 40 billion yen was speculative.
"The report was speculation by Nihon Keizai and we have not decided anything about such things," a spokesman for the major Japanese realtor said.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun's Thursday edition said Mitsui's current loss for 1996/97 to next March would result from sales of unprofitable properties. But it said the firm would a post net profit as it would post special profits of 50 billion yen from the sale of shares it holds in Oriental Land Co Ltd, the operator of Tokyo Disneyland.

Mitsui is considering cutting its debt on which it has to make interest payments but has not decided any details, the spokesman said. Such debts totalled 1.29 trillion yen at the end of March against sales of 664 billion yen in 1995/96.
Nihon Keizai said the sale of unprofitable real estate and Oriental Land shares will help the company cut such debt.

Some analysts said Mitsui Fudosan was expected to sell shares in Oriental Land in 1996/97 in order to cover losses stemming from the sale of unprofitable real estate. However, it is not realistic to estimate the company would earn profits of 50 billion yen from the sales in 1996/97, they said.
"We expect Mitsui will use the capital gains from the Oriental Land share sales, but it is not known whether the company has decided to post a parent current loss," one said.
Brokerage officials have said Oriental Land would go public and list its shares on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in mid-December, but the company has declined to comment.
Mitsui Fudosan owns 31.78 million shares of Oriental Land with a book value of 2.1 billion yen, the spokesman said.
